newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR sees sugar industry shake-up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR sees sugar industry shake-up.

text.p: Australian sugar giant CSR Ltd said on Friday the sugar industries of Australia and New Zealand required restructuring in light of high losses.

CSR's managing director Geoff Kells said he thought all the major players, including CSR, Mackay and the minor New South Wales sugar producers, "would be doing a lot of thinking on restructuring alternatives"

Speaking to Reuters at the opening by Prime Minister John Howard of a new CSR fibre cement plant in the western Sydney suburbs, Kells was asked to comment on rumours that CSR could merge with or take over rival Mackay Refined Sugars Pty Ltd.
He said: "What my comment would be is: the losses in refined sugar in Australia and New Zealand are now very high and clearly restructuring in the industry is necessary.
"And I think all major suppliers -- New South Wales, Mackay, CSR -- would be doing a lot of thinking on restructuring alternatives. Beyond that I can't comment."

He was asked if there should therefore be a restructuring. "Well there's no question. At the moment prices are very low, so what will cause the prices to move to more normal levels? You would have to say some restructuring," he said.
"There are many issues in restructuring; there are competition issues, there are commercial issues, export issues, so I prefer not to talk about that".
A merger proposed three years ago was blocked by the Trade Practices Commission, a predecessor to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
Kells declined all comment on legal action by Mackay against CSR subsidiary New Zealand Sugar Corp seeking about NZ$10 million in damages for alleged predatory pricing.
Mackay said on Monday it had launched the action.
Mackay is a joint venture between international commodities firm E D & F Man and the Mackay Sugar Co-operative.
